evals.prompt:
# Minottobot audit — Swiftly Inc — 2026-08-17

## Repos in scope
- Swiftly monolith (Node.js API + React frontend + PostgreSQL)

## Phase 0 baseline
- Team size: 4 engineers (3 backend, 1 frontend), no dedicated QA
- Total tests: 0 — team keeps saying they'll write them, but hasn't
- CI run time: ~2 minutes (GitHub Actions, ESLint only)
- Deployment frequency: 2-3 times per day via `git push heroku main`, manual
- Incidents: roughly 1 per day, almost always reported by users first. MTTR ~1 hour
- Code review: informal, no policy

## Area scores (1 = critical · 5 = excellent)
| Area                    | Score | One-line finding                     |
|-------------------------|-------|--------------------------------------|
| CI/CD                   | 2/5 | Runs lint only, no test gate, manual deploy |
| Testing                 | 1/5 | Zero tests of any kind |
| Code review             | 2/5 | No formal policy, informal only |
| Monitoring              | 2/5 | No error tracking, incidents found by users |
| Developer Experience    | 2/5 | No staging environment, manual heroku deploys |
| Ownership & culture     | 3/5 | Small team, everyone engaged, no structural gaps found |

## Evidence & red flags
- No staging environment — every change goes straight to production
- Zero automated tests despite 2-3 daily deploys
- Incidents (~1/day) are caught by users before the team notices

## Systems flagged for replacement evaluation
- None — the gap is absence of tooling, not a system to replace
evals.expected_output: An improvement plan that gives at least one short-term testing action item, recommends a specific test type to start with (not just 'add tests'), and does not recommend a full test suite rewrite as the first step.
assertions: Output must give at least one short-term action item related to testing
Output must recommend a specific test type to adopt first, not just 'add tests'
Output must not recommend a full test suite rewrite as the first step
Output must carry forward the CI/CD score of 2/5 and the Testing score of 1/5 from the audit input without changing them

evals.name: enterprise-legacy
evals.prompt:
# Minottobot audit — FinanceCore Ltd — 2026-08-17

## Repos in scope
- FinanceCore platform (Java Spring Boot microservices, Oracle DB, React frontend)

## Phase 0 baseline
- Team size: 85 engineers across 8 product teams, central QA guild of 6
- Total tests: ~12,000, approximately 30% flaky and frequently ignored
- CI run time: 47 minutes (Jenkins, set up in 2011, maintained by a dedicated CI team)
- Deployment frequency: biweekly release window, 6-hour deployment with manual sign-offs
- Incidents: 2 P1/month, 1 P2/month, MTTR ~4 hours
- Code review: 3 required approvals, formal policy, skipped for 'hotfixes' by some teams

## Area scores (1 = critical · 5 = excellent)
| Area                    | Score | One-line finding                     |
|-------------------------|-------|--------------------------------------|
| CI/CD                   | 2/5 | 47-minute Jenkins build, maintained by dedicated CI team |
| Testing                 | 2/5 | ~30% of 12,000 tests are flaky and ignored |
| Code review             | 2/5 | Formal policy bypassed for 'hotfixes' |
| Monitoring              | 3/5 | MTTR ~4 hours, no further detail provided |
| Developer Experience    | 2/5 | Slow 47-minute feedback loop, biweekly release window |
| Ownership & culture     | 3/5 | Central QA guild exists, no structural red flags found |

## Evidence & red flags
- 47-minute CI run time on Jenkins is the single largest feedback-loop cost
- 30% flaky test rate is a trust problem, not just a coverage gap — the team already ignores failures
- Code review policy has a formal 'hotfix' bypass that some teams use routinely

## Systems flagged for replacement evaluation
- Jenkins — set up in 2011, maintained by a dedicated CI team, 47-minute build time
evals.expected_output: An improvement plan that gives at least one short-term action item, addresses the 30% flaky test rate as a trust issue, and — if it recommends replacing Jenkins — states the migration cost and risk in the same recommendation.
assertions: Output must give at least one short-term action item
Output must address flaky tests specifically (not just 'tests exist')
Output must not recommend replacing Jenkins without acknowledging migration cost
Output must carry forward the CI/CD score of 2/5 from the audit input without changing it

evals.prompt:
# Minottobot audit — Norsk Mobility AS — 2026-08-17

## Repos in scope
- Norsk Mobility platform (Python + Django backend, React Native mobile app, PostgreSQL)

## Phase 0 baseline
- Team size: 14 engineers + 2 dedicated QA
- Total tests: 340 unit, 45 integration, 12 E2E — all E2E written in the last week, previously zero
- CI run time: ~12 minutes (GitHub Actions, manual approval gate before production deploy)
- Deployment frequency: 1-2 times per week
- Incident: 4 days ago, a race condition in the payment processing service corrupted payment records for 2,100 users. Data partially recovered, investigation ongoing
- Monitoring: Sentry added 3 days ago; before that, nothing — users reported issues directly

## Area scores (1 = critical · 5 = excellent)
| Area                    | Score | One-line finding                     |
|-------------------------|-------|--------------------------------------|
| CI/CD                   | 3/5 | 12-minute run, manual approval gate before prod |
| Testing                 | 3/5 | 397 tests total, but E2E coverage only exists since last week |
| Code review             | 3/5 | No data suggesting problems, none reported |
| Monitoring              | 2/5 | Sentry added only 3 days ago, after the incident |
| Developer Experience    | 3/5 | No major DX gaps reported |
| Ownership & culture     | 3/5 | No structural red flags found |

## Evidence & red flags
- 4 days ago, a race condition in the payment processing service corrupted payment records for 2,100 users; investigation ongoing
- Monitoring (Sentry) was only added 3 days ago, reactively, after the team had no visibility during the incident

## Systems flagged for replacement evaluation
- None
evals.expected_output: An improvement plan that explicitly references the recent incident and the race condition, recommends monitoring/observability as a priority, gives at least one short-term action item, and does not recommend 'psychological safety' as an action unless directly supported by a specific data point.
assertions: Output must reference the recent production incident explicitly
Output must give at least one short-term action item
Output must recommend monitoring or observability as a priority
Output must not recommend psychological safety without citing a specific data point
Output must reference the race condition or production data corruption

# Minottobot audit — Atmos (Helix team) — 2026-08-17

## Repos in scope
- Helix platform (TypeScript + Next.js + Supabase)

## Phase 0 baseline
- Team size: 7 engineers, no dedicated QA — quality is everyone's job
- Total tests: 2,100 unit, 380 integration, 85 E2E
- CI run time: 8 minutes (GitHub Actions, required to pass before merge, no exceptions)
- Deployment frequency: 4.2 deploys/day on average, all behind feature flags, automatic rollback on error spike
- Incidents: 0.1 P1/month, 0.5 P2/month, MTTR 12 minutes
- Monitoring: Datadog with custom SLOs per service, full on-call rotation with runbooks
- Code review: 1 approval required, PRs consistently have substantive discussion

## Area scores (1 = critical · 5 = excellent)
| Area                    | Score | One-line finding                     |
|-------------------------|-------|--------------------------------------|
| CI/CD                   | 5/5 | 8-minute build, no-exceptions merge gate |
| Testing                 | 4/5 | 2,565 tests across all layers, healthy pyramid shape |
| Code review             | 4/5 | Substantive review on every PR |
| Monitoring              | 5/5 | Datadog with custom SLOs, full on-call rotation |
| Developer Experience    | 4/5 | 4.2 deploys/day behind feature flags, auto-rollback |
| Ownership & culture     | 4/5 | No structural red flags found |

## Evidence & red flags
- Incident rate is genuinely low: 0.1 P1/month, 0.5 P2/month, MTTR 12 minutes
- No missing tooling identified — Datadog, feature flags, and SLOs are already in place

## Systems flagged for replacement evaluation
- None
evals.expected_output: An improvement plan that acknowledges the genuinely low incident rate (0.1 P1/month), does not recommend tools the team already has (e.g. Datadog, feature flags), and includes at least one non-trivial medium or long-term recommendation rather than being purely congratulatory.
assertions: Output must acknowledge the low incident rate of 0.1 P1/month
Output must not recommend tooling the team already has (e.g. Datadog, feature flags, SLOs)
Output must give at least one non-trivial medium- or long-term recommendation
Output must include at least one genuine improvement item, not purely congratulatory content

evals.name: org-chaos
evals.prompt:
# Minottobot audit — Momentum Fintech (Platform team) — 2026-08-17

## Repos in scope
- Momentum Fintech Platform (PHP + Laravel monolith, Node.js microservices, MySQL)

## Phase 0 baseline
- Team size: 11 engineers on paper, 4 on loan elsewhere — 7 effectively active
- Total tests: ~800, not run in about 2 months, current pass rate unknown
- CI: two systems — CircleCI (original) and GitHub Actions (added 6 months ago), no authoritative one identified
- Deployment frequency: irregular, last deploy 3 weeks ago
- Incidents: not formally tracked; a major outage 6 months ago is still not fully resolved
- Code review: officially required, skipped whenever something is 'urgent'
- Org: 3 VPs of Engineering in the last 18 months, no product owner currently assigned

## Area scores (1 = critical · 5 = excellent)
| Area                    | Score | One-line finding                     |
|-------------------------|-------|--------------------------------------|
| CI/CD                   | 2/5 | Two CI systems (CircleCI and GitHub Actions), no authoritative one |
| Testing                 | 2/5 | ~800 tests unrun for 2 months, pass rate unknown |
| Code review             | 2/5 | Formal policy routinely skipped for 'urgent' work |
| Monitoring              | 2/5 | Incidents untracked, 6-month-old outage unresolved |
| Developer Experience    | 3/5 | No specific DX complaints beyond process gaps above |
| Ownership & culture     | 2/5 | No product owner assigned; 3 VPs of Engineering in 18 months; 4 of 11 engineers on loan |

## Evidence & red flags
- Ownership is structurally absent: no product owner, 3 VPs of Engineering in 18 months, headcount on paper (11) exceeds effective capacity (7)
- Two CI systems (CircleCI and GitHub Actions) coexist with no authoritative one for deployments
- A major outage from 6 months ago remains unresolved and untracked alongside other incidents

## Systems flagged for replacement evaluation
- CircleCI or GitHub Actions — the team runs both and cannot name which is authoritative for deployments
evals.expected_output: An improvement plan that explicitly addresses ownership ambiguity as a root cause, names both CI systems (CircleCI and GitHub Actions) as a concrete problem, gives at least one actionable short-term item that can be done despite the organisational chaos, and does not recommend a full team reorganisation.
assertions: Output must address ownership ambiguity explicitly
Output must mention both CI systems by name (CircleCI and GitHub Actions)
Output must give at least one short-term action item that is actionable despite the chaos
Output must not recommend a full team reorganisation
Output must carry forward the Ownership & culture score of 2/5 from the audit input without changing it
